For more information on Hitachi, please visit the company's website at https://www.hitachi.com.
Summary
Hitachi America, Ltd. (http://www.hitachi-america.us/) has an opening for a Research Science Intern in the Financial Innovation Laboratory (FIL) located in Silicon Valley. We work on a variety of research problems, many of which involve AI. Our research is practical, with the goal of addressing customer pain points; however, like academia we publish as well. IP generation (patents etc.) are encouraged.
 We are seeking a research science intern to create innovative algorithms and solutions. The successful candidate will have an opportunity to solve challenging real-world problems, work on large data sets and to build practical solutions with the guidance of experienced scientists. This position is a perfect match for an enthusiastic learner who is passionate about using machine learning/AI/data mining/statistics to create a better society.
As an intern, you will be assigned to one or more projects, which best fit your skills, interests, and personality. You will be paired with a mentor to guide you, and you will gain practical knowledge while advancing cutting-edge solutions. We expect you to be productive, proactive, and a team player.
More information about the research done at the laboratory can be found at:
http://www.hitachi-america.us/rd/
Responsibilities:
Research and develop innovative algorithms and solutions for finance, insurance, and the Internet of Things.
Prepare and execute proof-of-concepts of the solutions in collaboration with other researchers.
Publish technical results in leading conferences and file patents.
Qualifications:
Ph.D (or a Ph.D candidate) in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Quantitative Finance, Operational Research, or related field will be considered for a research intern role. Non-Ph.Ds with strong track records may be considered for a research developer intern role.
Strong research experience in artificial intelligence, machine learning, financial mathematics etc.
Good programming skills and knowledge of data science tools and libraries in Python (highly preferred) or similar.
Self-motivated and passionate about solving real-world problems and building innovative systems with big data analytics.
Experience with multicore programming and databases is a plus.
Experience with building processes and deploying codes on cloud platforms is a plus.
Knowledge of time series analysis techniques is a plus.
Demonstrated ability to effectively create and deliver technical communications, including patent applications, presentations, papers, and reports.
Ability to collaborate successfully with R&D co-workers.

Disasters move through a lifecycle: preparedness, response and recovery, with mitigation running underneath all three. ICF's Emergency and Disaster Management practice works across that entire lifecycle for federal, state and local government clients, organized into three service lines: Preparedness and Insurance, Emergency and Disaster Operations, and Disaster Recovery. This internship rotates an undergraduate student through all three, so the arc of a disaster (the planning before, the operations during and the rebuilding after) is something they see connected, not siloed.
Our summer internship is full-time for 10-weeks beginning in early June and ending in early August. Work may be performed in a hybrid capacity from Baton Rouge, LA or Tallahassee, FL, or remotely from any U.S. location. At this time, we are unable to provide relocation nor housing assistance.
The Rotation Experience
This is a learning and exposure focused internship, not a placement into one function. Interns move through each service line on a set rotation and work alongside the consultants doing the work that day.
Preparedness and Insurance (Planning)
This rotation sits on the front end of the lifecycle, before a disaster hits. Interns gain exposure to emergency operations plan development, hazard and vulnerability assessments, and exercise design across tabletop, functional and full scale formats used to test those plans. Additionally, Long term recovery planning that helps a jurisdiction come back stronger than before. Interns will also see how insurance and risk transfer strategies, including catastrophe modeling and risk pooling, factor into a client's broader resilience posture.
Emergency and Disaster Operations
This rotation sits inside active response. Interns gain exposure to Emergency Operations Center structure and staffing, Incident Command System and National Incident Management System practices, resource typing and mutual aid requests, and the situational awareness products, such as situation reports and leadership briefings, that keep a response moving and stakeholders informed.
Disaster Recovery
This rotation picks up once the response phase winds down and communities begin to rebuild. Interns gain exposure to FEMA Public Assistance program delivery, damage assessment, documentation, cost recovery and grant compliance.
Specific tasks and projects will vary by rotation and current caseload. This internship is not a guarantee of hands on ownership of any particular project. What is guaranteed is exposure, learning and time with the teams doing the work.
Basic Qualifications:
By start date at least 30 credit hours in emergency management, homeland security, public administration, political science, public health or a related field
U.S. Citizenship is required per Federal contracts
Preferred Qualifications:
Basic familiarity with the disaster lifecycle and core emergency management concepts is a plus, including coursework or self study in FEMA's Incident Command System or National Incident Management System (for example IS 100 and IS 700)
FEMA online coursework completed including FEMA IS-100.C, FEMA IS-200.C, FEMA IS-700.B, FEMA IS-800.D
Comfortable with Excel, PowerPoint and Word; exposure to GIS or other data analysis tools is a plus
Strong writing and research skills, including the ability to translate technical material for different audiences
Genuine interest in emergency management, disaster recovery or public sector consulting

Technical Learning & Application
Develop working knowledge of NXP product portfolios (MCUs, MPUs, wireless connectivity, analog, power management) and their applications

Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field
Rising junior, senior, or graduate student — expected graduation between December 2027 and June 2029
Cumulative GPA of 3.0/4.0 or higher
Authorization to work in the United States (no sponsorship available for intern roles)
Availability for 12 weeks full-time during Summer 2027 (May–August)
Preferred Qualifications
Coursework or project experience in embedded systems, analog/digital circuits, wireless communications, or power electronics
Familiarity with microcontrollers, FPGAs, or relevant development boards (e.g., Arduino, Raspberry Pi, STM32)
Exposure to programming languages such as C, C++, or Python
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and/or Google Workspace tools

You are curious about technology and genuinely interested in how semiconductor solutions solve real-world problems

Submit your application through NXP's careers portal at nxp.com/careers. Include your resume, unofficial transcript, and a brief statement (200–300 words) describing your interest in technical sales and a technology problem you find compelling.

Projects will be focused on improving quality, minimizing processing steps, increasing yield, and/or reducing hazards for manufacturing processes related to organic synthesis, biochemistry, and reagent formulations. Whether you’re working in our four global Home Offices, Distribution Centers or Retail Stores—TJ Maxx, Marshalls, Homegoods, Homesense, Sierra, Winners, and TK Maxx, you’ll find abundant opportunities to learn, thrive, and make an impact. Come join our TJX family—a Fortune 100 company and the world’s leading off-price retailer.

Opportunity to make an impact and contribute to a specific team
Volunteer, executive-led speaker series, and networking events
Challenging, collaborative, team-based environment
Inclusive culture where all Associates feel welcome, valued, and engaged
Career growth opportunities – with successful completion of this experience, you may be presented a future offer to return to TJX!

What you will do:
The TJX Supply Chain & Logistics teams provide supply chain expertise and solutions to support our global business. Focused on our direct and indirect supply chain, our goal is to successfully deliver product (merchandise) to our stores timely, efficiently, and in the most cost-effective manner. We partner across TJX to drive and enable supply chain strategies, encouraging collaboration and sharing of ideas to support the growth of our fast-paced business.
Logistics Analysts provide business and project support for critical supply chain initiatives. You will be assigned projects that contribute to the overall supply chain strategy, as well as assist with daily activities within the supply chain functions. You will collaborate with experienced team members to manage and execute projects and deliverables.
Depending on your interests, expertise, and our business needs, you could focus on one of several areas:
Our Business Enablement Team serves as the information and communication bridge between external vendors, internal partners, and logistics. They develop and execute innovative solutions to ensure merchandise arrives at stores most efficiently and in a cost-effective manner.
Our Strategy & Analytics Team provides analysis, reporting, and project management support to strategic, cross-functional initiatives and helps drive cost savings, service, and quality. They also manage Logistics systems, maintain models and data to provide insights for strategic decision making.
Our Inbound Operations Team manages the flow of goods from domestic and international vendors to a variety of facilities in the TJX U.S. network, utilizing our Transportation Management System (TMS) and other systems. They identify solutions for late containers and loads, secure cost-effective capacity strategies, and maintain provider relationships.
Our Outbound Operations Team stewards the flow of merchandize from Distribution Centers and Processing Centers to the TJX Stores nationwide, planning cross-dock loads and store deliveries via our Transportation Management System (TMS). They lead continuous improvement initiatives across the outbound network and maintain provider relationships.
Our Engineering Team designs, buys, builds and supports the material handling systems that move freight through the TJX US distribution network.

We are looking for students who are highly motivated self-starters and who possess the ability to prioritize effectively, be proactive and flexible, and thrive in a fast-paced, professional environment.

Current Juniors (December 2027 or May 2028 Graduates)
Students pursuing a Bachelor’s Degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Logistics, Industrial Engineering, Business Admin, or related major
Desire to pursue a career in Supply Chain / Logistics at TJX
Additional qualifications include:
A genuine interest in Supply Chain and Logistics
Problem solving through thinking analytically and creatively
Excellent communicators who work well in teams
Curiosity and eagerness to learn
Leadership abilities, relationship building, and excellent work ethic
Flexible and adept at handling change

Virtual, one-way interview (HireVue)
Two virtual behavioral interviews
Potential Internship Offer to join the TJX Family
With corporate offices located in Framingham and Marlborough, MA, and Distribution Centers in Woburn and Worcester, MA, reliable transportation is required as TJX is not easily accessible to public transportation. A variable, hybrid work schedule is part of the role based on the needs of the business.

Summer PhD Intern: Sr. Data Scientist
Day in the Life of Walmart Global Tech
If you’re thinking scale, think bigger and don’t stop there. At Walmart Global Tech, we don’t just innovate, we enable transformations across stores/clubs and different channels for the Walmart experience. We innovate to deliver a simple and seamless experience for our customers and members. Our tech talent solves the biggest and most complex problems. We drive digital transformation where data and analytics are enabling us to better serve our customers/members and create a digital relationship with them. As our customers/members evolve and adapt, we are taking it a few notches further here. We are changing what customers and members can expect from the experience of shopping, from the physical stores/clubs, to mobile, social, and even online; were not just ready for the future of shopping, we are creating it.
About Our Program:
Each summer, we select the best and brightest to look under the hood of the worlds largest retailer at our Walmart Home Offices across multiple locations. During the 11-week program, our interns work directly with teams who are changing the way the world shops. This is the beginning of what could be an exciting career with Walmart!
The intern experience includes: An impactful individual project designed to align to your skillsets and interests
Direct access to leadership across the enterprise
Executive-led speaker sessions with insightful Q&A
Community outreach events
Networking and social events
Learning & development opportunities targeting both hard and soft skills
Deep dives into different areas of our business
Time management and leadership development as a full-time associate
An in-depth look at our Belonging, Culture of Belonging () practices
Compensation and housing assistance provided
Roles & Responsibilities:
Applied Business Acumen Identifies and helps design solutions to business problems based on machine learning and other advanced algorithms
Owns delivery of the piece of the project assigned by the broader team
Helps define measurement and implementation plans to unlock business value
Problem Formulation Translates problems that need solving into algorithmic solutions
Gains expertise in the domain area to identify the boundaries of the problem and helps design a strong solution for it
Data Source Identification Works with product and data experts to explore various datasets and identify those most appropriate
Builds data quality checks to ensure the integrity of data pipelines used in the solution
Model Analysis Owns technical solution development, learning requirements and best practices from the team
Leverages exploratory data analysis techniques to understand the data
Defines and engineers features, builds and evaluates simple models, then adds complexity to modeling as needed
Drives measurement of the solution
Model Assessment & Validation Supports model fit testing and statistical inference to evaluate performance
Assesses the impact of variables and features on inference results and business outcomes.
Model Deployment & Scaling Writes production-ready analytical models and data pipelines
Gains experience in production support, using those skills for evaluations, tracking, and alerting of key KPIs
Code Development & Testing Develops code according to project requirements, in the recommended language
Modifies and enhances code based on code reviews
Implements unit tests, integration tests, and code quality checks to ensure quality deployments
Data Visualization Creates visualizations for key datasets and models to highlight contributions made to the project and team
Presents innovative ideas to collaborators using appropriate graphing libraries and BI tools
Develop insights about model health, data quality, and business processes to meet customer needs
Office Environment: Corporate
U.S. Tech Hub Location(s): Bentonville, AR & Sunnyvale, CA
*Location availability is limited based on job profile and business needs.
Desired Majors: Computer Science, Data Science, Machine Learning, Analytics, Mathematics, Statistics, or other relevant majors
Minimum Qualifications Must be enrolled in a PhD degree program currently
Expected graduation date between December 2027-August 2028
0-1 years of relevant full-time experience (excludes internship and research-based roles)
Housing and relocation available for those living outside a 50-mile radius of the Walmart Home Office.

We’re Watts. Together, we’re reimagining the future of water.
We feel proud every day about what we do. We're all part of the same crucial mission, no matter what function we support -- it's to provide safe, clean water for the world, and to protect our planet's most valuable resource.
What we do:
For 150 years, Watts has built best-in-class products that are trusted by customers in residential and commercial settings across the world. We are at the forefront of innovation, working with cutting-edge technology to provide smart and connected, sustainable water solutions for the future. Watts is a leading brand with a quality reputation — and we have a dynamic future ahead.​
The Watts Internship Program is your chance to bring what you’ve learned in the classroom to life! You’ll dive into real-world projects, gaining hands-on experience while learning how business really works from the inside. During the program, you’ll get to roll up your sleeves and make an impact on day-to-day operations. Plus, you'll have tons of opportunities to network with passionate professionals across manufacturing, industrial engineering, and more—sparking new ideas through cross-department collaboration. It’s all about expanding your skills, challenging yourself, and exploring where your ambitions can take you!
Scope of Position
This innovative and detail-oriented individual, as part of the Operations team, will support the identification and implementation of shop floor process improvements aimed at increasing efficiency, reducing costs, and enhancing production output. The Manufacturing Engineering Intern will work with cross-functional teams to support continuous improvement initiatives and gain hands-on experience with manufacturing processes.
This position reports to the Senior Manager of Advanced Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement. This role is onsite and is based in St. Pauls, NC.
Primary Job Duties and Responsibilities
Help create and maintain shop floor work instructions, including specifications, engineering changes, process controls, and tooling requirements.
Participate in lean manufacturing initiatives that support continuous process improvement.
Collaborate with hourly employees and teams across Quality, Safety, Sourcing, and other functions on manufacturing projects.
Support the scoping, planning, and execution of manufacturing engineering requests under the guidance of the Manufacturing Engineering team, including improving manufacturing efficiency, implementing engineering changes, improving product quality, and addressing production line technical issues.
Analyze and document existing manufacturing processes to identify improvement opportunities.
Support Watts’ commitment to continuous improvement by identifying process inefficiencies, communicating findings transparently, and taking accountability for assigned project deliverables.
Assume responsibility for other projects and duties as assigned by the Manufacturing Engineer Manager or Company management.
Required Qualifications
Current student (sophomore, junior or senior status).
Pursuing a degree in Manufacturing, Mechanical, or Industrial Engineering.
Ability to present complex data effectively through charts, tables, graphs, and pivot tables.
Ability to work independently and manage assigned tasks with appropriate guidance.
Ability to communicate professionally and effectively with colleagues across departments and levels of the organization.
Passionate about your work, with a genuine desire to contribute meaningfully and make an impact.
Demonstrated commitment to integrity and respect in interactions with others, fostering a positive and inclusive work environment.
Strong sense of accountability, taking ownership of tasks and following through on commitments.
Understanding of and adherence to applicable laws, codes, policies, regulations, and safety practices and procedures, as applicable.
Must be authorized to work in the United States without requiring sponsorship now or in the future.
Must successfully establish employment eligibility and satisfactorily complete background checks, including required pre-employment testing as a condition of employment.
Preferred Qualifications
Knowledge of Lean manufacturing principles.
Familiarity with quality standards and process improvement methodologies, such as Six Sigma.
General Applicable Company Competencies
Commitment to Watts’ values of integrity, accountability, continuous improvement and innovation, and transparency.
Punctuality and dependability.
Ability to be flexible and adapt to changing work priorities and stressful conditions.
Adherence to all personnel policies, procedures, and standards of process as implemented by Watts.
Maintain productive and collaborative relationships with other Watts employees.
Adherence to Watts’ seven cultural beliefs: Growth Mindset, Customer-Focused Innovation, Constant Communication, Clear Goals, Collaborate Globally, Be Inclusive, and Take Action.
Working Conditions
While performing the job duties, you will be working on-site at a manufacturing facility and will perform the majority of your duties in an office environment. You may, at times, be required to be present on the manufacturing floor and will be required to wear the appropriate personal protective equipment. You will be required to work in the office at the St. Pauls, NC location (Monday–Friday). Your scheduled work hours will be communicated to you by your manager.
Physical Requirements
Specific physical abilities required for this position include, but are not limited to:
Ability to remain seated at a desk or workstation for extended periods.
Ability to physically move around the office, organize or transport files, packages, or other office-related materials.
Ability to read documents, use a computer, and perform data entry tasks.
Ability to communicate clearly with management and coworkers, particularly in meetings or phone calls.
Ability to operate standard office equipment such as computers, printers, phones, and copiers.
Ability to stand for long periods of time.
Ability to lift and carry up to 20 pounds.
Ability to push and pull up to 20 pounds.
Ability to physically move around the manufacturing floor.
Ability to read documents and communicate clearly with management and coworkers.
Ability to wear personal protective equipment, which may include, but is not limited to, safety shoes, hearing protection, and safety glasses.
Pay Range: $21-27
The expected hourly range for this position is $21–27 hourly. Actual compensation will be dependent upon individual skills, experience, qualifications, and applicable law.
What’s In It for You
People-First Culture – Enriching and caring for people is at the core of who we are; this includes executing our Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) strategy, and providing you with meaningful career growth opportunities, a positive and safe work environment, and affirmation that you are heard, valued, and respected.
Flexible PTO Policy – Work-life balance is important at Watts and our interns receive one (1) hour of flexible PTO for every thirty (30) hours worked. Your flexible PTO can be utilized for any type of absence.
Paid Holidays – Celebrate the holidays with your loved ones and still get paid! You will receive the following paid holidays off during your time as an Intern with Watts. Where a holiday falls during the weekend, it will be observed on an adjacent weekday.
Lunch and Learns – Throughout your internship, there will be opportunities for you to sign up to learn and network with some of the key strategic leaders and thought partners within our core operating model!
Sustainability – For five years in a row, Watts has been named one of "America's Most Responsible Companies" by Newsweek. Join our journey as we continue to distinguish Watts as a responsible and committed corporate citizen.
